# agentbox **English** · [Bahasa Indonesia](README.id.md) **Claude Code and Hermes Agent, running right on your Android phone.** agentbox is a [KernelSU](https://kernelsu.org) module that sets up a real Linux system (Void Linux, glibc) inside your phone and runs **[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)** and **[Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent)** there as a regular, safely confined user. Set it up once, and your AI agents live in your pocket, start when the phone boots, and are reachable over Telegram, a terminal, or a chat app. ![arm64](https://img.shields.io/badge/arch-arm64-informational) ![KernelSU](https://img.shields.io/badge/KernelSU-module-success) ![Void Linux](https://img.shields.io/badge/rootfs-Void%20Linux%20glibc-478061) ![offline WebUI](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebUI-offline-blueviolet) [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/rjial/agentbox?include_prereleases)](https://github.com/rjial/agentbox/releases) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](LICENSE) > **Language note:** the WebUI and CLI messages are currently in Indonesian. Button labels below are quoted > as they appear on screen, with an English translation. --- ## Why agentbox? - **No emulation, no proot.** A chroot with KernelSU root: native speed and a real glibc, so the official Claude Code and Hermes binaries run as-is, without Termux patches. - **An always-on assistant.** The Hermes gateway (Telegram and other platforms) runs under its own supervisor: it starts at boot, restarts itself with backoff if it crashes, and rotates its logs. - **Managed from the phone, no laptop needed.** A WebUI in KernelSU Manager covers status, the gateway, a terminal for setup wizards, and configuration. Sign in to Claude, install Hermes, set up Telegram, all from your phone screen. - **Secure by default.** The agents never run as root, have no sudo, and secrets never show up in logs or process arguments. - **One CLI for everything.** `agentbox setup`, `doctor`, `shell`, `update`, `backup`, and more. The WebUI calls the same CLI, so behavior is always consistent. ## Features ### One-shot, idempotent setup `agentbox setup` downloads the latest Void rootfs (checksum verified), installs base packages, creates the `agent` user, then installs Claude Code and Hermes through **their own official installers**. Every component records when it is done: setup is safe to re-run, and a failed step can be retried on its own. ``` rootfs → base → locale → user → claude → uv → hermes → gateway ``` ### WebUI in KernelSU Manager Four pages with bottom navigation, working fully **offline** (no CDN): | Page | What it shows | |---|---| | **Status** | What is installed or missing, Claude Code & Hermes versions, disk space, the next step | | **Gateway** | Start/stop/restart the gateway, start at boot, the last 200 log lines | | **Terminal** | A real terminal (xterm.js) for interactive wizards: Claude sign-in, `hermes setup`, `hermes model`, `gateway setup`, install/reinstall Hermes | | **Konfigurasi** (Configuration) | Hermes provider & model, masked keys with inline edit forms, credential status checked directly against Anthropic, the API key for the chat app | The WebUI terminal **opens no network port**. Input and output go through a FIFO and root-owned files, and only commands from a fixed list can run (there is no free shell). ### One Claude subscription sign-in, shared by both Have Claude Pro, Max, or Team? Sign in once in Claude Code (`claude auth login`), then a single tap on **"Pakai Claude"** ("Use Claude") on the Configuration page (`agentbox config hermes-link-claude`) makes Hermes use Claude models through the same sign-in, which refreshes itself automatically. Another Hermes provider is switched to Anthropic (default model `claude-sonnet-5`, the old `config.yaml` is backed up). No more copying tokens that expire or get truncated. `agentbox config auth-check` checks the credentials **actually in use** directly against Anthropic (free, no conversation is created) and catches classic mistakes such as an OAuth token stored in an API key variable. ### Chat from an Android app Turn on the Hermes **Gateway API Server** with one button, then connect the [hermes-android](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android) chat client to `127.0.0.1:8642`. The key is random (32 bytes), shown only on request, and can be rotated at any time. ### Diagnostics that tell you how to fix things `agentbox doctor` checks the architecture, rootfs, disk space, mounts, DNS, HTTPS/certificates, locale, the user, internet access as `agent`, tool versions, credentials, and the gateway. Every check prints **OK / WARN / FAIL** together with the command that fixes it. `doctor --fix` only applies safe fixes. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Android["Android (root via KernelSU)"] WebUI["WebUI
KernelSU Manager"] --> CLI["agentbox CLI"] Boot["service.sh
(at boot)"] --> SUP["gateway.sh
supervisor"] CLI --> SUP end subgraph Void["chroot Void Linux (glibc)"] Claude["Claude Code"] Hermes["hermes gateway
Telegram · API Server"] end CLI -- "su -l agent" --> Claude SUP -- "setpriv --reuid=agent" --> Hermes App["hermes-android app"] -- "127.0.0.1:8642 + API key" --> Hermes TG["Telegram"] <--> Hermes ``` - The rootfs lives in `/data/adb/agentbox/rootfs`, **outside** the module folder, so it survives module updates. - Your phone's internal storage appears as `/sdcard` inside the chroot, so Claude Code can work on your projects directly. ## Security This project is built on the assumption that AI agents run code, and that your phone holds important data. - **The agents are never root.** `claude` and `hermes` always run as the `agent` user (fixed uid 8061), without sudo and outside the `wheel` group. System packages can only be installed via `agentbox install`. - **The UID is chosen deliberately.** The default UID 1000 collides with Android's `AID_SYSTEM`, while UIDs ≥ 10000 are blocked by netd. The agent uses a range Android does not use, plus the network groups the Android kernel requires. - **Deleting never touches your storage.** `reset` and uninstall must unmount every bind mount and verify it through `/proc/mounts` before deleting anything, and they validate paths. - **Secrets never leak into logs or argv.** API keys are read from stdin or the environment, shown only masked (`sk-ant-…a1b2`), and config files are `600`. - **No unnecessary open ports.** The WebUI terminal opens no port. The Hermes API Server listens on loopback only and requires a key. The Hermes web dashboard is intentionally **not** enabled, because on Android loopback it has no login and could be taken over by other apps. ## Requirements - An **arm64** Android phone with **KernelSU** (developed and tested on KernelSU-Next). - A metamodule for the `system/bin` overlay (for example mountify). Without one, agentbox writes small launcher commands into Termux instead. - About **3 GB** free in `/data`, and an internet connection during setup. - A Claude account (Pro/Max/Team) or an Anthropic API key for Claude Code. Hermes can use any provider it supports. ## Installation 1. **Download the module zip** from [Releases](https://github.com/rjial/agentbox/releases): pick `agentbox-vX.Y.Z-release.zip` (or `-debug.zip` for full diagnostic logs). Verify it with the `SHA256SUMS` file from the same release. Or build it yourself (works on the phone via Termux, or on a PC): ```sh git clone https://github.com/rjial/agentbox.git cd agentbox sh tools/build.sh release # output: dist/agentbox--release.zip ``` 2. **Flash** the zip in KernelSU Manager, then reboot. 3. **Set up**, either way: - WebUI: KernelSU Manager → agentbox → **Terminal** → *setup (semua komponen)* ("setup, all components"), or - Termux: `su -c agentbox setup` 4. **Sign in and configure**: - Terminal → *login Claude Code*, tap the link, approve in your browser, and paste the code back. - Konfigurasi → *Pakai login Claude Code* ("Use Claude Code login") if Hermes uses Anthropic, or *hermes setup* for other providers. - Terminal → *gateway setup* for Telegram. The gateway is enabled at boot automatically. ## Everyday use ```sh claude # Claude Code in the chroot, as the agent user hermes # Hermes Agent agentbox shell # enter the chroot as agent (--root for repairs, --safe for rescue) agentbox doctor # full diagnostics agentbox config auth-check # Anthropic credentials in use, checked against the API agentbox service status # gateway status (start | stop | restart | log | autostart on|off) agentbox update # update the rootfs, Claude Code, and Hermes agentbox backup # archive /home/agent ``` `claude`, `hermes`, and `agentbox` can be called straight from Termux; when needed they elevate to root through `su` and then drop back down to the `agent` user. Every command has `--help`. ## Development ```sh sh tools/build.sh release # zip without debug logging sh tools/build.sh debug # zip with debug logging: logs/debug.log, setup trace, Hermes installer --verbose ``` - Android-side scripts are written in **POSIX sh** and must pass `shellcheck -s sh` with no warnings. Scripts inside the chroot may use bash (`shellcheck -s bash`). - The WebUI has no build step: plain HTML, CSS, and JS, with libraries in `webroot/vendor/` (xterm.js; Preact + htm on the Configuration page). - Architecture notes, design decisions, and verification results live in [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) (in Indonesian). ### Versioning and releases agentbox follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org). The version is written only in `module.prop` (`version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, with `versionCode = MAJOR×10000 + MINOR×100 + PATCH` so KernelSU always recognizes the newer version). Bump it with: ```sh sh tools/bump-version.sh patch # or minor | major | 1.2.0 | 1.3.0-rc.1 git commit -am "Release v0.1.1" && git push ``` Every push to `main` that changes the version runs [GitHub Actions](.github/workflows/release.yml): lint (shellcheck), version validation, release + debug zip builds, then a **GitHub Release** `vX.Y.Z` with `SHA256SUMS` and generated release notes. Pre-release versions (e.g. `-rc.1`) are marked as *prerelease*. ### Updates from KernelSU Manager `module.prop` includes `updateJson`, so KernelSU Manager checks for the latest stable release on its own and offers the update together with its changelog. Every stable release ships an `update.json` and a `changelog.md`; pre-releases are never offered as updates. The rootfs, configuration, and data in `/data/adb/agentbox` are left untouched when the module is updated. ## Status agentbox is used and tested on one device (arm64, KernelSU-Next). Some parts are still a **prototype**: - WebUI terminal: latency and the on-screen keyboard depend on the KernelSU Manager WebView on your phone. - The Configuration page is a Preact pilot; the other pages are still plain JavaScript. - The hermes-android app is a third-party project and has not been thoroughly tested with agentbox. Bug reports and pull requests are very welcome. ## Credits - [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) by Anthropic. Its binary is **not bundled**; it is always downloaded from the official installer during setup. - [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) by Nous Research, installed through its official installer. - [Void Linux](https://voidlinux.org), [xterm.js](https://xtermjs.org) (MIT), [Preact](https://preactjs.com) (MIT) + [htm](https://github.com/developit/htm) (Apache-2.0). Licenses for the bundled libraries are in `webroot/vendor/`. - [hermes-android](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android) by rusty4444. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 Rizal Abdul Basith. Third-party libraries in `webroot/vendor/` keep their own licenses (xterm.js MIT, Preact MIT, htm Apache-2.0). Claude Code and Hermes Agent are not part of this repository and are subject to their authors' licenses and terms.

---

Why agentbox?

  • **No emulation, no proot.** A chroot with KernelSU root: native speed and a real glibc, so the official

    • Claude Code and Hermes binaries run as-is, without Termux patches.

  • **An always-on assistant.** The Hermes gateway (Telegram and other platforms) runs under its own

    • supervisor: it starts at boot, restarts itself with backoff if it crashes, and rotates its logs.

  • **Managed from the phone, no laptop needed.** A WebUI in KernelSU Manager covers status, the gateway,

    • a terminal for setup wizards, and configuration. Sign in to Claude, install Hermes, set up Telegram, all

    from your phone screen.

  • **Secure by default.** The agents never run as root, have no sudo, and secrets never show up in logs or

    • process arguments.

  • **One CLI for everything.** `agentbox setup`, `doctor`, `shell`, `update`, `backup`, and more. The WebUI

    • calls the same CLI, so behavior is always consistent.

    Features

    One-shot, idempotent setup

    agentbox setup downloads the latest Void rootfs (checksum verified), installs base packages, creates the

    agent user, then installs Claude Code and Hermes through their own official installers. Every

    component records when it is done: setup is safe to re-run, and a failed step can be retried on its own.

    rootfs → base → locale → user → claude → uv → hermes → gateway

    WebUI in KernelSU Manager

    Four pages with bottom navigation, working fully offline (no CDN):

    | Page | What it shows |

    |---|---|

    | Status | What is installed or missing, Claude Code & Hermes versions, disk space, the next step |

    | Gateway | Start/stop/restart the gateway, start at boot, the last 200 log lines |

    | Terminal | A real terminal (xterm.js) for interactive wizards: Claude sign-in, hermes setup, hermes model, gateway setup, install/reinstall Hermes |

    | Konfigurasi (Configuration) | Hermes provider & model, masked keys with inline edit forms, credential status checked directly against Anthropic, the API key for the chat app |

    The WebUI terminal opens no network port. Input and output go through a FIFO and root-owned files, and

    only commands from a fixed list can run (there is no free shell).

    One Claude subscription sign-in, shared by both

    Have Claude Pro, Max, or Team? Sign in once in Claude Code (claude auth login), then a single tap on

    "Pakai Claude" ("Use Claude") on the Configuration page (agentbox config hermes-link-claude) makes

    Hermes use Claude models through the same sign-in, which refreshes itself automatically. Another Hermes

    provider is switched to Anthropic (default model claude-sonnet-5, the old config.yaml is backed up).

    No more copying tokens that expire or get truncated.

    agentbox config auth-check checks the credentials actually in use directly against Anthropic (free,

    no conversation is created) and catches classic mistakes such as an OAuth token stored in an API key

    variable.

    Chat from an Android app

    Turn on the Hermes Gateway API Server with one button, then connect the

    hermes-android chat client to 127.0.0.1:8642. The key is

    random (32 bytes), shown only on request, and can be rotated at any time.

    Diagnostics that tell you how to fix things

    agentbox doctor checks the architecture, rootfs, disk space, mounts, DNS, HTTPS/certificates, locale,

    the user, internet access as agent, tool versions, credentials, and the gateway. Every check prints

    OK / WARN / FAIL together with the command that fixes it. doctor --fix only applies safe fixes.

    How it works

    flowchart LR
  subgraph Android["Android (root via KernelSU)"]
    WebUI["WebUI<br/>KernelSU Manager"] --> CLI["agentbox CLI"]
    Boot["service.sh<br/>(at boot)"] --> SUP["gateway.sh<br/>supervisor"]
    CLI --> SUP
  end
  subgraph Void["chroot Void Linux (glibc)"]
    Claude["Claude Code"]
    Hermes["hermes gateway<br/>Telegram · API Server"]
  end
  CLI -- "su -l agent" --> Claude
  SUP -- "setpriv --reuid=agent" --> Hermes
  App["hermes-android app"] -- "127.0.0.1:8642 + API key" --> Hermes
  TG["Telegram"] <--> Hermes
  • The rootfs lives in `/data/adb/agentbox/rootfs`, **outside** the module folder, so it survives module

    • updates.

  • Your phone's internal storage appears as `/sdcard` inside the chroot, so Claude Code can work on your

    • projects directly.

    Security

    This project is built on the assumption that AI agents run code, and that your phone holds important data.

  • **The agents are never root.** `claude` and `hermes` always run as the `agent` user (fixed uid 8061),

    • without sudo and outside the wheel group. System packages can only be installed via agentbox install.

  • **The UID is chosen deliberately.** The default UID 1000 collides with Android's `AID_SYSTEM`, while

    • UIDs ≥ 10000 are blocked by netd. The agent uses a range Android does not use, plus the network groups

    the Android kernel requires.

  • **Deleting never touches your storage.** `reset` and uninstall must unmount every bind mount and verify

    • it through /proc/mounts before deleting anything, and they validate paths.

  • **Secrets never leak into logs or argv.** API keys are read from stdin or the environment, shown only

    • masked (sk-ant-…a1b2), and config files are 600.

  • **No unnecessary open ports.** The WebUI terminal opens no port. The Hermes API Server listens on loopback

    • only and requires a key. The Hermes web dashboard is intentionally not enabled, because on Android

    loopback it has no login and could be taken over by other apps.

    Requirements

  • An **arm64** Android phone with **KernelSU** (developed and tested on KernelSU-Next).
  • A metamodule for the `system/bin` overlay (for example mountify). Without one, agentbox writes small

    • launcher commands into Termux instead.

  • About **3 GB** free in `/data`, and an internet connection during setup.
  • A Claude account (Pro/Max/Team) or an Anthropic API key for Claude Code. Hermes can use any provider it

    • supports.

    Installation

  • **Download the module zip** from [Releases](https://github.com/rjial/agentbox/releases): pick

    • agentbox-vX.Y.Z-release.zip (or -debug.zip for full diagnostic logs). Verify it with the SHA256SUMS

    file from the same release.

    Or build it yourself (works on the phone via Termux, or on a PC):

    ```sh

    git clone https://github.com/rjial/agentbox.git

    cd agentbox

    sh tools/build.sh release # output: dist/agentbox--release.zip

    ```

  • **Flash** the zip in KernelSU Manager, then reboot.
  • **Set up**, either way:

    • - WebUI: KernelSU Manager → agentbox → Terminal → *setup (semua komponen)* ("setup, all components"), or

    - Termux: su -c agentbox setup

  • **Sign in and configure**:

    • - Terminal → *login Claude Code*, tap the link, approve in your browser, and paste the code back.

    - Konfigurasi → *Pakai login Claude Code* ("Use Claude Code login") if Hermes uses Anthropic, or

    *hermes setup* for other providers.

    - Terminal → *gateway setup* for Telegram. The gateway is enabled at boot automatically.

    Everyday use

    claude                      # Claude Code in the chroot, as the agent user
hermes                      # Hermes Agent
agentbox shell              # enter the chroot as agent   (--root for repairs, --safe for rescue)
agentbox doctor             # full diagnostics
agentbox config auth-check  # Anthropic credentials in use, checked against the API
agentbox service status     # gateway status             (start | stop | restart | log | autostart on|off)
agentbox update             # update the rootfs, Claude Code, and Hermes
agentbox backup             # archive /home/agent

    claude, hermes, and agentbox can be called straight from Termux; when needed they elevate to root

    through su and then drop back down to the agent user. Every command has --help.

    Development

    sh tools/build.sh release   # zip without debug logging
sh tools/build.sh debug     # zip with debug logging: logs/debug.log, setup trace, Hermes installer --verbose
  • Android-side scripts are written in **POSIX sh** and must pass `shellcheck -s sh` with no warnings.

    • Scripts inside the chroot may use bash (shellcheck -s bash).

  • The WebUI has no build step: plain HTML, CSS, and JS, with libraries in `webroot/vendor/` (xterm.js;

    • Preact + htm on the Configuration page).

  • Architecture notes, design decisions, and verification results live in [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md)

    • (in Indonesian).

    Versioning and releases

    agentbox follows Semantic Versioning. The version is written only in module.prop

    (version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, with versionCode = MAJOR×10000 + MINOR×100 + PATCH so KernelSU always

    recognizes the newer version). Bump it with:

    sh tools/bump-version.sh patch     # or minor | major | 1.2.0 | 1.3.0-rc.1
git commit -am "Release v0.1.1" && git push

    Every push to main that changes the version runs GitHub Actions: lint

    (shellcheck), version validation, release + debug zip builds, then a GitHub Release vX.Y.Z with

    SHA256SUMS and generated release notes. Pre-release versions (e.g. -rc.1) are marked as *prerelease*.

    Updates from KernelSU Manager

    module.prop includes updateJson, so KernelSU Manager checks for the latest stable release on its own and

    offers the update together with its changelog. Every stable release ships an update.json and a

    changelog.md; pre-releases are never offered as updates. The rootfs, configuration, and data in

    /data/adb/agentbox are left untouched when the module is updated.

    Status

    agentbox is used and tested on one device (arm64, KernelSU-Next). Some parts are still a prototype:

  • WebUI terminal: latency and the on-screen keyboard depend on the KernelSU Manager WebView on your phone.
  • The Configuration page is a Preact pilot; the other pages are still plain JavaScript.
  • The hermes-android app is a third-party project and has not been thoroughly tested with agentbox.

    • Bug reports and pull requests are very welcome.

    Credits

  • [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) by Anthropic. Its binary is **not bundled**; it is always

    • downloaded from the official installer during setup.

  • [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) by Nous Research, installed through its

    • official installer.

  • [Void Linux](https://voidlinux.org), [xterm.js](https://xtermjs.org) (MIT),

    • Preact (MIT) + htm (Apache-2.0).

    Licenses for the bundled libraries are in webroot/vendor/.

  • [hermes-android](https://github.com/rusty4444/hermes-android) by rusty4444.

    • License

    MIT © 2026 Rizal Abdul Basith. Third-party libraries in webroot/vendor/ keep their own licenses

    (xterm.js MIT, Preact MIT, htm Apache-2.0). Claude Code and Hermes Agent are not part of this repository and

    are subject to their authors' licenses and terms.
